clue.text: British graduate brought in special information document — it retains some point

indicators.note: something brought in is placed inside, so the graduate pieces go within the document word

parts.note: a card is a small document carrying information, like a business or ID card
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: An official files a special briefing paper after a British graduate submits it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a sheath holds the point of a sword, so 'point' is a blade's tip, not a purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath for a sword or dagger keeps the blade, tip included, covered and contained.

clue.text: Making 150 head away from audience

parts.note: CL is 150 in Roman numerals

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which goes away here

parts.note: an audience is a hearing, as in being granted a hearing

explanation.surface: A speaker moves the audience by keeping their head down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making' is a verb sense: clearing a sum means netting it, as in making a profit.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearing a sum means netting it as profit, just as making a sum does.

clue.text: Ray's about right for fish

indicators.note: about means going around, so the beam word wraps the right letter

parts.note: a ray of light is a beam

explanation.surface: A man called Ray is thought about the right sort of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like the flat fish, which sits nicely beside 'fish'; it is a beam of light.
explanation.definitionFit: The bream is a freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Play mate never getting up to mischief?

definitions.meaning: a comedy by Oscar Wilde, first staged in 1895

definitions.text: mate never getting up to mischief?
definitions.meaning: a perfectly behaved spouse, a partner without faults

explanation.surface: A playful partner who never gets into trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilde's comedy is so titled, and a flawless spouse is literally a model married man.

clue.text: Noblewoman, old, abandoning jet and ship

indicators.note: to abandon is to leave, so the old letter leaves the jet word

parts.note: a douche is a jet of water directed at the body
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: An elderly aristocrat gives up flying and travels by sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' removes O from DOUCHE, leaving DUCHE; 'jet' looks like air travel but is a spray of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A duke's wife or a woman holding a ducal title ranks high in the peerage.

clue.text: Support provided when apprehended by officer

indicators.note: apprehended means caught and held, so the officer letters hold the other piece

parts.note: Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant
provided means on condition that, which is if

explanation.surface: Backing is given only once a police officer catches a suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apprehended' suggests an arrest, but here it signals one piece held inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a lift is to raise or boost them, a form of support.

clue.text: Spectacles leg, rotten, twisted

indicators.note: twisted means bent out of shape, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pair of glasses with a decayed, bent arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leg' fits glasses, whose side arms are sometimes called legs, but it is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: These are eyeglasses held up by a long handle rather than resting on the ears.

clue.text: A lot of excellent beer in the end

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: fine means excellent, as in a fine wine
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Plenty of top-quality beer drunk at the close of the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: The last section of a show or piece of music is its close.

clue.text: Supports arrangement of date with current unwelcome controller

parts.note: to back is to support, so supports is backs

indicators.note: an arrangement puts the letters of date in a new order

parts.note: a river is a flowing current of water

explanation.surface: A sponsor sets up a date with an electricity supplier nobody wants in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks electrical but is a flowing body of water; 'arrangement of' gives EATD.
explanation.definitionFit: A passenger who keeps telling the driver how to drive is an unwanted would-be controller.

clue.text: One from Arabia, I will follow the old people

indicators.note: following means coming after, so I goes after the other pieces

parts.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the
men are people

explanation.surface: Someone from Arabia promises to follow the elders.
explanation.definitionFit: Yemen lies at the southern tip of the Arabian peninsula, so its citizens are Arabians.

clue.text: Series about former king produces discomfiture

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the series word goes around the king letters

parts.note: a chain is a series of linked events
GR, Georgius Rex, stands for a past King George

explanation.surface: A run of programmes about a deposed monarch causes embarrassment.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe vexation or embarrassment at being thwarted or humiliated.

clue.text: Positive about me before first performance

parts.note: re means about or concerning
mi, also spelt me, is the third note of the tonic sol-fa scale
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: An actor is upbeat about themselves before opening night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'me' is the sol-fa note, written MI here, not the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening night of a play or film is its debut showing.

clue.text: Encourage family hand-out, while giving nothing away

parts.note: kin are family

indicators.note: nothing is the letter O, and giving it away removes it

parts.note: the dole is a state hand-out to the unemployed

explanation.surface: Supporting relatives with charity while never parting with a penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving nothing away' takes O from DOLE, leaving DLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up or arouse a feeling, like lighting a fire, is to foster it.

clue.text: Laws actioned in error? Very apprehensive

indicators.note: in error means wrong, so the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Legal cases brought by mistake leave a lawyer nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking out in clammy perspiration from fear is an idiom for deep anxiety.

clue.text: Graceful when receiving crazy nut's insult

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the graceful word takes the other piece inside

parts.note: comely means attractive, graceful

indicators.note: crazy means wild, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the word nut, its possessive ending acting as a link

explanation.surface: An elegant person is slighted by a madman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' gives TUN, which 'when receiving' places inside the graceful word.
explanation.definitionFit: Contumely is scornful, abusive language or treatment, so an insult.

clue.text: Salt found in tree top

indicators.note: something found in another is inside it, so the salt formula goes within the tree

parts.note: the pine is a tree
NaCl is the chemical formula for common salt

explanation.surface: Salt crystals discovered at the top of a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinnacle is the summit or highest point of something.

clue.text: Cavorting in sauna there will give you an attack of nerves

indicators.note: cavorting means leaping about, so the letters jump into a new order

explanation.surface: Larking about in a sauna leads to nervous collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an old medical term for nervous exhaustion and its symptoms.

clue.text: Go to work for various employers, protected by attorney

indicators.note: something protected is surrounded, so the attorney letters go around the work word

parts.note: Att. is an abbreviation for attorney
to temp is to work for a series of employers on short contracts

explanation.surface: An agency worker gets legal cover from a lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a go at something means to try it.

clue.text: Think lake will contain small shellfish

indicators.note: to contain is to hold inside, so the think and lake pieces hold the small letter

parts.note: to muse is to think, ponder

explanation.surface: Imagine a lake holding small shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: A mussel is an edible bivalve mollusc with a dark shell.

clue.text: Problem in public transport when going round part of town

indicators.note: going round means turning about, so the combined letters run the other way
the problem word goes in, between letters of the transport word

parts.note: a bus is public transport
rub means problem, as in there's the rub

explanation.surface: Trouble on the bus as it circles one district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' gives BRUBUS, and 'going round' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: A residential district on the edge of a city is one part of the town.

clue.text: Successful concern involves Republican, I see

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap up inside, so the concern word holds the other letters

parts.note: a thing is a concern, as in it's my thing
v, from Latin vide, means see

explanation.surface: A prosperous company takes on a Republican, I notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is V, the Latin vide used in cross-references.
explanation.definitionFit: Thriving means flourishing, doing very well.

clue.text: Mercenary likely to be pardoned after one escapes

indicators.note: after one escapes reads as what is left once one has got away, so after frames the removal
escaping means getting out, so the letter for one leaves the pardon word

parts.note: a venial sin is a minor one that can be forgiven
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A hired soldier is set to be pardoned once a comrade gets away.
explanation.definitionFit: Venal means open to bribery, motivated purely by money.

clue.text: Bone not yielding useful material initially

parts.note: stern means firm, unyielding

indicators.note: initially points to the first letters of the two words useful and material

explanation.surface: A bone that resists giving up useful material at first.
explanation.definitionFit: The breastbone, the flat bone in the middle of the chest.

clue.text: Italian city wrong toimprison bridge opponents

indicators.note: to imprison is to shut inside, so the wrong word holds the bridge letters (the clue runs to and imprison together)

parts.note: a vice is a wrong, a moral failing
in bridge, East and North are opposing players, E and N

explanation.surface: It is wrong to lock up one's bridge rivals in an Italian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Venice is the canal city in north-east Italy.

clue.text: Former college having a change of heart in scheme

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, and those middle letters change places

parts.note: a poly, or polytechnic, is a former type of British college

explanation.surface: An old college rethinks its plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having a change of heart' swaps the middle two letters O and L. Polytechnics were UK colleges turned into universities in 1992.
explanation.definitionFit: A ploy is a cunning tactic or stratagem.

clue.text: Mystery movie perhaps has farm worker throttling personnel

indicators.note: throttling grips around the neck, so the farm worker surrounds the personnel letters

parts.note: a tiller is one who tills the soil
HR, human resources, is the personnel department

explanation.surface: A film where a farmhand strangles the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throttling' grips round the neck, so it signals one piece wrapped round another.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspense film or crime mystery is a typical example of the genre, hence 'perhaps'.
